newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos says the successsful hosting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings will bring in more business and jobs to the Filipino people (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Left-wing labour leader Filemon Lagman is released from military custody after a Quezon city court rules that his detention on a four-year old murder charge is unlawful and illegal. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- President Fidel Ramos says the government is not abandoning its claim over the disputed isles and atolls in Spratlys Islands in the south China sea (TODAY)
- The National Power Corp announces a 10-centavo per kilowatt hour increase in power rates for Luzon users. (MALAYA)
- Philippine trade officials are said to be amenable to accepting the U.S. offer of increasing the country's garments export quota, industry officials say. (INQUIRER)
- The presidential palace downplays allegations that the new excise tax law on beer and cigarettes is not valid. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The legislative bicameral committee discussing proposed amendments to the expanded value-added tax law is prepared to finalise the measure within two weeks, Senate president Ernesto Maceda says (BUSINESS DAILY)
- The government posts a budget surplus of 6.85 billion pesos in the first ten months of the year as against a 10.065 billion peso surplus recorded during the same period last year. (BUSINESS STAR)
